title: indigo_mount_synscan: X_MOUNT_USE_ENCODERS treats encoder counts as motor steps and re-bases the step counter (AZ-GTi)
description:
Found on 2026-11-19 while working on ticket 4ef695f1-88ae-4fd8-943e-91c6479a9c24, measured by direct UDP commands on an AZ-GTi (firmware 3.16, CPR 2073600, extended status =098000); not yet reproduced through the driver.

Observations:
- The ':d<axis>' reply (auxiliary encoder) counts about 1068 per revolution, the step counter ':j<axis>' 2073600 (ratio 1941.57; DEC quarter turn: j2 518400, d2 267). The protocol document in the repository gives no encoder resolution and no query for it.
- With X_MOUNT_USE_ENCODERS on, synscan_update_axis_positions() reads ':d' instead of ':j' and uses the value as motor steps, so the published coordinates cannot be right on this mount.
- Enabling the dual encoders (':W<axis>040000', sent by the X_MOUNT_USE_ENCODERS handler) makes the firmware re-base the step counter from the encoder at once: with the mount standing, j1 went from -66767 to -2576467. The axis reference of the session is lost and stays lost after the encoders are disabled again.

To do: reproduce through the driver on the AZ-GTi with the same scenario (coordinates and step counters before / after switching the item on and off, then a GoTo), compare with the behaviour of mounts whose encoders count in steps if one is available, and decide with the owner what X_MOUNT_USE_ENCODERS should do on mounts whose encoder resolution differs from the step counter (scale by a measured ratio, hide the item, or refuse). X_ENCODER_POSITION (raw counts, driver 3.0.0.23) is not affected. Driver version to be incremented with the fix; recorded simulator and hardware runs.

outcome.summary:
Reviewed master...HEAD (ae4f10ec5, merge base 2a91e57eb). The change implements the owner's option 1 correctly; no blocking defect.

Verified:
- Version 30 -> 31. The generated .c has DRIVER_VERSION 0x0300001F. The unchanged generator, run in scratch, reproduces .c/.h/_main.c byte for byte, and the .c diff against master holds exactly the .driver diff plus the version define.
- synscan_update_axis_positions() always reads :j. The 'd' branch and the *_axis_position_from_encoder fields are gone. synscan_read_encoder_position() always queries :d, so X_ENCODER_POSITION is unchanged; the encoder_position cases pass.
- Every other user of positions works in steps: park save/restore (:E plus a park file of :j values, checked by keeps_side_of_pier_and_park_in_steps), side of pier, sync (alignment model only) and auto home. Auto home turns the encoders off at its start, clears the items and ra_encoder/dec_encoder, and defers an X_MOUNT_USE_ENCODERS change while it runs, all consistent with synscan_set_encoders().
- synscan_set_encoders() sends :W..04/05; the items and private flags show what the controller accepted.
- on_change then calls synscan_update_mount_coordinates() on the master queue. Its state is BUSY while a slew or home runs or a request is claimed (on_change_request claims SLEWING/sync_pending at admission), otherwise OK. A kept ALERT is preserved by indigo_update_coordinates(). Client targets are untouched and there are no foreign-frame values.
- Connect: :W is sent only when the property is visible (hidden when no axis reports the encoder bit, so no :W there), after :F/:E and before the first :j. A failed :W sets ALERT and the connection survives unless the port is lost. Sending :W..05 at connect cannot re-base: the firmware re-bases only on enable, per the phase 1 hardware note, and phase 2 found coordinates matching :j after the connect-time :W05.
- Simulator: --encoder-offsets defaults to 512,1024 (the old array values), and the re-base happens only on :W..

Phase 1 reproduction through the driver (3.0.0.25, ae5a33f77) on the AZ-GTi, firmware 3.16, synscan://192.168.111.139:11880, 2026-11-21 09:38-09:44 CET, site 48.1/17.1, no alignment points, SLEW mode. A baseline off: RA 1.3507 DEC 60.963, j1 -480194 j2 351953, d1 -267 d2 181. B GoTo 1.5 deg off: j moved +8622/-8640, d -263/177, coordinates = target. C X_MOUNT_USE_ENCODERS on (driver sends :W1040000, :W2040000): j1 re-based at once -471572 -> -510633 (= -263 x 1941.57, -39061 steps, -6.78 deg), j2 unchanged (difference to d2 x 1941.57 was 345 steps, under one count); published RA 19.828 DEC -0.039 (d read as steps) against true RA 1.27 DEC 59.46. D guarded 1.5 deg GoTo on: driver moved the axes correctly by :j, reported OK at RA 19.845 DEC -0.0385 for a target RA 1.6428 DEC 60.967. A GoTo to the displayed coordinates would have moved +88.6/-59.6 deg (predicted only, not run). E off: no re-base back; coordinates from j again but 6.76 deg off in RA axis. F GoTo off back to the B position: d -263/177 as at B, published RA differs from B by 0.450 h minus LST change = 6.76 deg: reference stays lost. No documented read-only query reports the encoder resolution (a,b,D,g,s,c,i,m answered, q 000000 and k unknown); 2073600/1941.57 = 1068 counts/rev. Restored: :E1 with +39061 (this also re-based d1 -263 -> -242), then GoTo to j1 -480197 j2 351953; X_MOUNT_USE_ENCODERS and the firmware dual encoder left off; d1 now -246 instead of -267 at the original pointing. Legacy driver before 49acc55af only sent :W04/05 and always read :j.

Reproduced on the AZ-GTi (see note). What should X_MOUNT_USE_ENCODERS do? Option 1 (recommended): restore the pre-3.0 meaning - the item only switches the firmware dual encoders (:W04/05), positions are always read with :j, never :d as steps; simulator models the re-base. Option 2: scale :d by a per-model ratio. Option 3: hide/refuse the item.

- Simulator: --encoder-offsets defaults to 512,1024 (the old array values), and the re-base happens only on :W..04 with --encoder-counts, so default behaviour is unchanged.
- Park path fix: the driver's file is indigo_uni_config_folder()/synscan-EQ8.park = HOME/.indigo. The old helper removed nothing. The existing callers remove the file in cleanup after a park, and the driver itself deletes the file on connect, so no case depended on the file surviving; 123/123 recorded.
- PROPERTIES.md text is accurate, no property added or removed. MIGRATION_STATUS 121 -> 123 (123 cases registered), Comment column untouched. README and TEST_SUMMARY change only the record line. No library or generator change. Formatting is fine and git diff --check is clean.

Scratch copy, ticket driver: the 4 new cases, the handshake and the 5 encoder_position cases PASS. Master's driver compiled against the same test: all 4 new cases and the handshake FAIL (pointing moved by the :d offsets / :d read as steps / no connect-time :W); the encoder_position cases still PASS. The new cases are event-driven (property revisions, polls, GoTo completion); the 3 s sleep helper was removed.

For the owner (behaviour, not a defect): every connect now sends the item's value. A new driver, or one whose item is off, turns OFF dual encoders that were enabled elsewhere, for example AZ-GTi Freedom Find from the SynScan app. Legacy only sent :W on change. This is documented in PROPERTIES.md and is the price of the item matching the unqueryable controller state, but the owner should confirm it.

Minor, not blocking:
(1) The simulator's rebase_from_encoder() and the test replay round the steps up (ceil) for positive counts, which keeps the encoder reading. Their comments say 'rounded towards zero', true only for negative counts; the hardware measurement was trunc, a 1-step difference.
(2) The old comment 'The :d reading of an axis ...' now sits above encoder_ticks() instead of encoder_reading().
(3) The simulator's :E does not resync the encoder as the AZ-GTi does (phase 2 note); no case depends on it.
(4) synscan_set_encoders() addresses both axes even when only one reports an encoder, as on_change already did; on such a mount every connect could leave the property ALERT. Hypothetical, no such model known.

Master's reject_change 'Mount is homing' and the BUSY guard do not interact with this change: X_MOUNT_USE_ENCODERS has its own auto-home deferral and the coordinates publication goes through the same state rules as the poll.
